episode.title: Building A $50K Coaster Cabin From Scratch! ✨

synopsis: A playful mountain cabin integrated with a functional wooden coaster track around its roof and deck is built on a pine hillside.

shots.prompt:
A fresh exterior scene in a wide view whose position and angle stay fixed, with a slow zoom as its single movement. An empty lot is graded, then road, fence and landscaping are laid out, then the foundation is marked. The builder arrives with materials.

A sloping mountain clearing among tall pine trees is leveled with wooden retaining walls. Heavy cedar timber posts and bent wood coaster track segments arrive on a rugged mountain trailer.

The same fixed exterior view continues from the previous final frame, with a slow zoom as its single movement. Foundation, walls and roof frame rise inside that same composition with accelerating timelapse energy and satisfying material flow.

Heavy timber posts anchor into concrete footings. Wall frames and roof trusses rise rapidly while curved wooden track supports extend outward from the cabin eaves across the hillside terrain.

The same fixed exterior view continues from the previous final frame, with a slow zoom as its single movement. Cladding, roof, paint, exterior lighting and landscaping are finished until the completed exterior stands clearly in frame.

Cedar lap siding covers the walls, durable metal roofing caps the pitch, and polished timber coaster tracks loop seamlessly around the wrap-around porch and roof overhangs amidst fresh pine landscaping.

A fresh interior wide scene whose position and angle stay fixed, with a slow zoom as its single movement. Interior walls go up, flooring is laid, utilities and lighting infrastructure are installed, carrying the exterior's materials and design language inside.

Inside the open cabin space, wide plank oak flooring installs across structural floor joists. Exposed timber roof trusses receive warm recessed lighting fixtures, and plumbing lines route through timber wall studs.

The same fixed interior view continues from the previous final frame, with a slow zoom as its single movement. Furniture and decor are installed, the lighting comes up, and the interior is finished until it looks ready to live in.

A rustic stone hearth is built against the side wall. Leather armchairs, a carved timber dining table, and warm Edison bulb pendants create an inviting alpine interior living space.

Continuing from the previous final frame, the viewpoint is released for one unbroken move that begins inside, passes through a door or window, and settles on a wide exterior of the finished structure while the builder keeps working.

Gliding smoothly from the warm living room, the movement passes through double glass doors onto the wooden deck, revealing the full playful coaster cabin architecture as the builder polishes the coaster rail.

music: Upbeat acoustic guitar plucking paired with lively wooden percussion, stomps, and snare rims. The energetic beat mirrors the playful construction flow. At the conclusion of shot 5, the instrumentation drops to a quiet acoustic strum, opening into a joyful, sweeping timberland melody for shot 6, ending softly.
